provider: Kaggle Notebook outputs (/kaggle/working) — the free side-channel

free_tier.stated: Up to 20 GBs of output from a Notebook may be saved to disk in /kaggle/working. This data is saved automatically and you can then reuse that data in any future Notebook

per_object_cap.notes: Up to 20 GBs of output from a Notebook may be saved to disk in /kaggle/working. This data is saved automatically and you can then reuse that data in any future Notebook

retention.stated: A Notebook version is a snapshot of your work including your compiled code, log files, output files, data sources, and more.
retention.notes: Additional scratchpad disk space (outside /kaggle/working) that will not be saved outside of the current session

egress.terms: Free download of notebook output files from the version's Output tab, same GCS-backed delivery.

interface_detail: This is a command-line interface tool for interacting via commands in a terminal or shell script
tooling: kaggle CLI (`kaggle kernels output <owner>/<kernel> -p ./dir`) and kagglehub. The notebook executes on managed GPU and TPU compute, writing files directly on the host without local upload transfer.
chaining: By chaining Notebooks as data sources in this way, it’s possible to build pipelines and generate more and better content than you could in a single notebook alone.
limits_note: 20 GB per version is hard; 9 h / 12 h session limits per run; output is only persisted on commit ('Save & Run All'), not on interactive save; GPU/TPU hours are rationed (~30 h/week) but CPU-only runs are not the constraint for pure storage.
reliability_note: Outputs persist indefinitely and are downloadable years later; the flaky part is the commit step (a timed-out run loses the output).
confidence_note: The Kaggle notebooks documentation was read on 2026-11-09 and states the auto-saved output allowance.
